A Tuber (Japanese: うきわボーイ Inner Tube Boy and うきわガール Inner Tube Girl) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that debuted in the Generation III games. They are young children in inner tubes that are learning to swim. They come in male and female versions. They appear to be younger versions of s. The prize money for defeating them is generally low.

When male Tubers are paired with female Swimmers in Double Battles, they are called s.

They generally use a combination of and —particularly , , and their related forms.

==In the manga==
 
===Pokémon Adventures===
==== ====
In Pinsir Me, I Must Be Dreaming, faces a virtual female Tuber at the . She also appears in a flashback in Verily Vanquishing Vileplume I.

==== ====
In Magnificent Meditite & Really Riolu I, a Tuber makes a cameo while the main characters visit Veilstone City. His friend was supposed to challenge Maylene but she mixed the Tuber and his friends with the three main characters, due to the main characters possessing an item that made landing attacks easier she had heard the kids talking about.

The Tuber and his friend appeared briefly in Stunning Staravia & Stinky Skuntank II, noticing the impact from the cannon.

In Double Trouble with Dialga and Palkia V, the Tuber and his friends were teleported to the Jubilife Grand Hotel due to the distortion of time and space.

==== ====
The Tuber from Magnificent Meditite & Really Riolu I is seen again together with his friends, entering the in Deprogramming Porygon-Z.
 

====Pokémon====
 

 

 

 

==Trivia==
In , there are no male Tubers, and the male version of the Trainer class is not even programmed into the games, despite there being a Trainer class (which is a female paired with a male Tuber).
In the Generation IV Battle Frontier, male Tubers use the Ninja Boy overworld sprite, while female Tubers use the Twins overworld sprite.
